newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU deficit target 3.0 pct-France's Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: EMU deficit target 3.0 pct-France's Arthuis.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Tuesday that the target for budget deficits as a percentage of gross domestic product in the Maastricht treaty on monetary union was 3.0 percent.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, he had been asked exactly what the target was in the treaty for allowing countries to join monetary union in 1999. Asked if it was 3.0 percent, he said: "Yes, 3.0 percent."

The Maastricht treaty allows for the trend towards three percent to be taken into account in judging readiness for monetary union, fueling speculation about whether or not a deficit of up to say, 3.4 or 3.5 percent would be acceptable.
Arthuis also said he hoped as many countries as possible would join economic and monetary union in 1999.
He had been asked whether or not Italy would qualify to join the euro currency at its launch.
"We need the most members in the euro area on January 1, 1999. We trust Italian authorities," he said.
He gave no further details on this, but said Europe would in any case "have to support monetary stability" between the euro and currencies of countries waiting to join.
